newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine international reserves at $9.7 bln.
newsitem.headline: Philippine international reserves at $9.7 bln.

text.p: The Philippines' gross international reserves had gone down to $9.7 billion as of Monday morning, Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas Governor Gabriel Singson said.
Singson said the level was similar to the level registered in May last year. The reserves reached as high as $12 billion in March.

The central bank's reserves, which is comprised of gold, foreign currency and short-term dollar-denominated securities, were whittled down in the first ten days of the month due to persistent speculative attack on the peso.
Singson said it had sold a total of $1.58 billion between July 1 to July 10 to defend the peso.
On July 11, the central bank announced a de facto devaluation by allowing the peso to trade at a wider range and not intervening in the market.
Singson said he would not hesitate to use interest rates to temper wild fluctuations in the foreign exchange market.
